name: TX-30
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by about 25 points after redistricting
Haynes has raised roughly 26 times more than Jackson, with $200,000 in outside support
Prediction markets price the Democratic nominee near 97 percent
No public general-election polling, so the forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The open seat's D+25 lean, Haynes's overwhelming fundraising advantage, and market pricing near 97 percent all point the same direction, with no evidence on the other side of the ledger.
model.watch: A large polling miss in urban Texas or a sudden influx of Republican outside spending could narrow the expected margin, though not enough to threaten the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-30 is an open seat in Dallas, left vacant by the retirement of its longtime incumbent and redrawn as a strongly Democratic district. The fundamentals point firmly toward the Democratic nominee, Frederick Haynes III, in a seat that favored Democrats by roughly 25 points at the presidential level.

Haynes has raised about $657,000, more than twenty-five times the $25,000 taken in by Republican Everett Jackson, and outside groups have spent around $200,000 backing Haynes while leaving Jackson unopposed on the airwaves. Prediction markets give the Democratic nominee roughly a 97 percent chance of victory. With no public polling in the race, the forecast rests on the district's lean, the money gap, and market pricing, all of which align. The expected margin is about 26 points for the Democrat.
